I read 140 cards: 70 true and 70 false, 5 of each per section. Statement length is balanced: in every section the true and false averages are within 5 characters (closest call is 1.3 with 81.2 true vs 76.4 false). Across the deck the averages are 85.2 true and 84.3 false; explanations average 103 true and 108 false. Hedge verbs are roughly balanced ('can' appears in 9 true and 7 false). The tells come from false-statement templates and from key names:

1) Scope creep, where a setting or permission 'also' does a neighbouring thing. 7 cards, all false, no true counterpart: s2.1-04 (copies steps 'as well'), s3.3-05 ('also gives'), s4.1-04 ('also admits'), s4.1-07 (policy 'sends secrets'), s4.2-05 (runner group 'grants' IP allow list access), s5.1-01 ('adds scopes'), s5.1-03 (id-token 'gains write access'). 'also' is false 2/2, 'grants' false 2/2, 'admits'/'gains' false only. This breaks the rule of at most two false cards per template.

2) Precedence claims where the general or default value wins. 4 false: s1.3-08 (retention-days 'overrides' the org maximum), s3.2-02 (default 'overrides' with), s3.1-10 (entrypoint 'ignored'), s4.3-04 (repository secret 'wins').
